We are looking for a Financial Controller to lead the operational and analytical work behind our monthly close, group consolidation, project controlling and control environment of a fast-growing energy trading and technology group – and to rebuild them AI-first, so our numbers are faster, more reliable and ready for scale.

Why this role matters

Hybrid Greentech is scaling fast as a VPP, BRP and electricity retailer across Denmark, and Northern Europe. Energy trading means large and volatile daily revenue, cost and cash transactions – so quality , accuracy and liquidity control are not back-office topics; they decide how fast we can grow. This role exists to give management, the board and investors numbers they can trust, on time, and to build controls and automation that scale with the business rather than with headcount. The same discipline is needed in our consultancy arm, where technical consultants deliver advisory and EPC management projects: clear project economics, timely invoicing and early warning when a project drifts.

The role

As Financial Controller, you report to our Finance Manager and work closely with the CFO and our accountant in a small, hands-on finance team. You lead the operational and analytical work within the financial steering, reporting and finance and business analytics; running the month-end close, the consolidation of our group entities in Denmark and abroad, balance sheet reconciliations, project controlling and the day-to-day operation of our internal controls. This is an individual contributor role with high ownership and direct visibility towards management.

You will work in close collaboration with our settlement team, project managers and business owners to ensure adequate financial steering and reporting, partner with our accountant on more complex accounting topics, and work across trading, portfolio management, commercial and engineering. We are a tech-first company with high AI adoption, and we expect you to work that way too: AI tools, scripting and automation are your default approach to removing manual work from close, reconciliation and reporting – combined with the judgement to know when a number needs a human review.

What you will do

• Lead and execute the monthly close and group consolidation, including account mapping, intercompany eliminations, reconciliations and variance analysis, and prepare the monthly financial and business review for the CFO, management and the board.

• Set up and run project controlling – project budgets, hours and utilisation, work in progress, milestone and fixed-fee revenue recognition and timely invoicing – giving project managers and business owners clear steering on margin, estimate-to-complete and cash.

• Automate and rebuild our reporting flow – from ERP trial balances to consolidated P&L, balance sheet and cash flow – using AI tools, scripting and data pipelines, replacing manual spreadsheet steps with controlled, repeatable and documented processes.

• Operate and strengthen our internal controls within the framework set by the Finance Manager, including segregation of duties, payment and bank authorisations and documented business procedures, and drive follow-up on auditor recommendations.

• In close collaboration with Settlement, ensure trading-related balances – settlement, imbalance costs, customer prepayments and deposits, and collateral posted to TSOs, DSOs and exchanges – are correctly recognized, invoiced and reconciled

• Support cash and liquidity forecasting and management with the Finance Manager and CFO, including rolling cash forecasts, collateral and trading risk capital tracking, and early warning on cash exposure.

• Prepare and analyse the annual budget and monthly forecast updates for the Finance Manager and CFO, maintaining our driver-based budget model and following up on budget-versus-actual deviations with business owners.

• Handle key accounting areas such as revenue recognition and accruals, capitalisation of development projects, grant periodisation and month-end cost accruals, collaborating with our accountant on more complex accounting topics.

• Support in the year-end close and audit for all group entities, including annual reports, tax specifications and intercompany agreements, in close collaboration with Finance Manager and our external auditors.

• Work closely with our Settlement team and business owners to ensure adequate financial steering and reporting – turning data into insight on gross profit by revenue stream, cost of execution and unit economics, and building dashboards that let the business self-serve.

What you bring

Experience and skills (Required)

• 5+ years of experience as a controller, in audit or in a group finance role, ideally in a multi-entity set-up.

• A relevant degree in accounting, finance or economics (e.g. cand.merc., HD-R or cand.merc.aud.).

• Proven hands-on experience running month-end close, consolidation and year-end audit under the Danish Financial Statements Act (Årsregnskabsloven)

• Hands-on experience with ERP systems, preferably e-conomic

• Solid understanding of balance sheet accounting, revenue recognition, capitalised development costs, accruals and intercompany transactions.

• Experience with project controlling – budgets, work in progress, utilisation and project margin follow-up – ideally in a consultancy, engineering, Trading or EPC business.

• A genuine AI-first way of working: you use AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot daily and can show concrete examples of finance processes you have automated (e.g. with Python, SQL, Power Query, APIs or low-code tools).

• Strong Excel and financial modelling skills combined with a structured, control-minded approach and high attention to detail.

• The ability to work independently in a fast-paced scale-up, prioritise under pressure and explain financial matters clearly to non-finance colleagues.

• Language: English (required); Danish

Nice to have

• Experience from energy trading, utilities, commodities or financial services – e.g. settlement, collateral, imbalance or margin processes.

• Experience with e-conomic, time registration or PSA tools, ERP migration to a more scalable platform, and BI tools such as Power BI.

• Experience with public grant-funded projects, transfer pricing or building internal controls in a growth company.

• A background from a Big 4 or mid-tier audit firm.

What we offer

• Real responsibility: the chance to improve how close, controls and reporting are run in a scaling energy trading group – not just maintain them.

• An AI-first workplace where you get the tools and the mandate to automate, experiment and rethink how finance is done, working closely with our CFO, trading and tech teams with exposure to board and investor reporting.

• Competitive compensation and performance-based incentives.

• A collaborative environment with short decision lines, high trust, and strong cross-functional execution.

• The opportunity to work with forward-looking customers and partners driving electrification and the green transition in Northern Europe.

Ready to apply?

Ready to build an AI-first finance function for a company where every megawatt-hour traded must be settled, reconciled and controlled? If you combine accounting rigour with a builder's mindset, we would love to hear from you.

Deadline

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis until 10 December. We reserve the right to close this vacancy earlier if a suitable candidate is identified and accepted.

About Hybrid Greentech

Hybrid Greentech helps Battery Energy Storage Systems and flexible assets perform across their full lifecycle, from project readiness to real-time multi-market trading. We are a vertically integrated VPP, BRP and retailer. We combine analytics, EPC management, asset integration and automated trading to turn flexibility into reliable value for the grid and for asset owners. We are a diverse, international team of 45+ based in Høje Taastrup, building technology that makes 100% renewable energy workable in practice.

atNorth is a leading Nordic data center company providing cost-effective, scalable high-density colocation and built-to-suit services to industry-leading organizations across Iceland, Sweden, Finland, and Denmark.

With sustainability at our core, our data centers run on renewable energy and are designed according to circular economy principles. Through innovative design, power efficiency, and intelligent operations, we deliver reliable, secure, and high-performance infrastructure.

Headquartered in Reykjavik, Iceland, atNorth operates eight data centers across the Nordics, with additional sites under development in Finland, Denmark, Sweden and Norway.

We combine world-class technology with a people-first culture built on collaboration, ownership, and trust, empowering our teams to grow, take responsibility, and make a real impact.

By joining our international team, you will help shape the future of sustainable digital infrastructure.

**Strategy Manager at atNorth

**Are you passionate about building strategy?

We are looking for a Strategy Manager to help define and drive atNorth's future growth and strategic direction. This is a highly visible role working closely with the CEO, Executive Committee, Board, and senior business leaders to identify opportunities, solve complex business challenges, and ensure atNorth remains at the forefront of the rapidly evolving Nordic data center market.

Focusing heavily on strategy development, you will lead analyses, challenge assumptions, identify opportunities, and develop recommendations that influence critical decisions across growth, power, sustainability, commercial development, and corporate strategy. Reporting to the Director of Strategy and working as part of our Strategy team, you will collaborate closely with our existing Strategy Manager, combining strategic thinking with practical execution to turn ambitious goals into tangible outcomes.

This is a unique opportunity to influence the direction of one of the fastest-growing data center platforms in the Nordics. You will have direct exposure to executive leadership and play a key role in decisions that shape the future of sustainable digital infrastructure across the region. You'll join a collaborative, international team where curiosity, ownership, and impact are valued, and where your work will directly contribute to atNorth's continued success.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Lead the development and refinement of atNorth's corporate strategy, ensuring alignment with long-term business objectives.

• Keep a pulse on market trends, customer demand, competitor activity, technology developments, and broader industry dynamics to identify risks and opportunities.

• Translate market insights and business intelligence into strategic recommendations that support growth, competitiveness, and long-term value creation.

• Partner with executives, business leaders, and functional teams to evaluate strategic initiatives and priorities across the organisation.

• Support strategic planning, decision-making, and Board preparation activities alongside the Executive Committee and senior leadership team.

• Lead strategic projects and cross-functional initiatives from concept through implementation.

• Develop compelling business cases, market assessments, and strategic presentations for senior stakeholders.

• Support the development of power, sustainability, commercial, and geographic growth strategies that are critical to atNorth's long-term success.

• Engage with internal and external stakeholders to gather insights that inform strategic planning and decision-making.

• Act as a trusted advisor and thought partner to senior leadership on strategic opportunities and challenges.

**Your profile:

**

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, Strategy, Industrial Management, or a related field.

• 5+ years of experience in corporate strategy, management consulting, business development, strategic planning, or related disciplines.

• Demonstrated experience developing business strategies and influencing strategic decisions at a senior level.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to turn complex information into actionable recommendations.

• Experience presenting to executive leadership teams, boards, or senior decision-makers.

• Excellent stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence without direct authority.

• Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to engage audiences ranging from operational teams to executives.

• Professional proficiency in English.

• Experience within the data center, energy, utilities, infrastructure, technology, or other capital-intensive industries is considered a strong advantage.

**About the atNorth Culture

**We believe that sustainable success starts with the wellbeing of our people. For us, an open, transparent, and inclusive culture is more than a priority, it is the core of how we lead and innovate.

We don’t just talk about culture; we nurture it. Through regular one-to-one engagements and monthly wellbeing surveys, we listen carefully to our teams, ensuring that every voice is heard and every opportunity for improvement is embraced.

We recognize that innovation and collaboration thrive where people feel truly connected, which is why we come together each week to share ideas, strengthen relationships, and nurture a sense of belonging, sometimes over a simple breakfast and good conversation.

At atNorth, we are building a community where you can do your best work and shape a sustainable future together.

At Cellerator, the partnerships you will build make life-changing therapies possible. We are a philanthropic organisation founded and funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, dedicated to turning cell-based therapies into treatments that reach the people who need them.

About the role

As our Business Development Specialist, you will turn interest from biotechs, spin-outs, academic groups and pharma into well-qualified programmes and signed agreements. You will assess scientific and strategic fit, guide clients through intake and due diligence, and shape proposals and deals. This is consultative business development, not hard selling. Just as importantly, you will design the commercial engine itself: the client journey, funnel, stage gates, CRM, pitch and pricing.

You will join a supportive team that values collaboration as we build the site together. If you are excited to shape how a new cell therapy facility partners with academia and industry from day one, this is the opportunity for you.

What you'll do

• Drive the funnel from first contact to signed agreement and a smooth handover to the Program Director and Project Manager, managing several opportunities at a time

• Assess the scientific, technical and strategic fit of programmes together with the Program Director and our Process Development and GMP experts, and lead intake and due diligence

• Build proposals and deals, including scope, assumptions, pricing input and timelines, and take them through contracting (NDA, MSA, SOW) with Legal and Finance

• Design and continuously improve our sales process and client journey: pipeline, lead criteria, stage gates, workshops, pitch materials and pricing models

• Own pipeline management and CRM, and work with Communications on campaigns, events, content and the website, so that marketing feeds the funnel

• Build long-term relationships with founders, academic teams, biotechs, pharma, investors and ecosystem partners, and represent Cellerator at events in the Nordics and Europe

What you'll bring

• An MSc in life sciences or a related field, with a strong understanding of drug development. Experience within cell or gene therapy is highly valued (PhD is an advantage)

• Around 8–10 years of professional experience, including solid experience in commercial or business development roles in drug development – ideally from a CDMO, CRO or biotech.

• The scientific credibility to understand cell therapy programmes and translate technical considerations into commercial discussions

• Experience working with structured sales processes, funnels or client journeys, combined with the ability and motivation to help build and improve our commercial setup.

• Hands-on experience with CRM, structured pipeline management and contracts such as MSAs, SOWs and change orders (SAP experience and an understanding of demand generation and marketing are an advantage)

• Excellent English, written and spoken (Danish and a network in the Nordic or European cell therapy ecosystem are an advantage)

• An entrepreneurial, consultative people person who builds trust quickly, is credible with scientists and executives alike, and is comfortable designing structure in an organisation that is still taking shape

Interested?

Send your CV and a short note about why this role interests you. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so do not wait for the deadline.

Life at Cellerator

We’re building something meaningful from the ground up. If you thrive in complexity, value pragmatic solutions over perfect theory, and want your work to directly influence how advanced therapies reach patients, you’ll feel at home here.

Built with you, not before you. We’re a scale-up, so our processes, culture, and ways of working are still taking shape. You won’t inherit a rigid playbook—you’ll help create it.

Work well, sustainably. We take work–life balance seriously and aim for a supportive, enjoyable workplace. Good science happens when people feel trusted, supported, and able to do their best work.

Flat by design. We work across teams rather than in silos. Whether you’re collaborating with GMP production, academic partners, or leadership, your perspective matters. We prioritise partnership over hierarchy.

Backed, but independent. The Novo Nordisk Foundation provides the stability and credibility to deliver on our mission. At the same time, our culture and direction are distinctly our own, and we move with the pace and spirit of a scale-up.

Board Intelligence is a technology and advisory firm on a mission to make boards more effective, and through them, build better businesses and benefit society.

Over twenty years we have established ourselves as the market leader in governance and board effectiveness, trusted by more than 80,000 directors, executives, and governance professionals globally, including across the Fortune 500, FTSE 100, and OMX 30. That trust has been earned through depth of insight, rigorous advisory work, and a track record that newer entrants simply cannot replicate.

We have invested in applied AI since 2020, well ahead of the market, and that early conviction has paid off. Our AI-powered platform and smart board advisor give us a competitive advantage that is widening, not narrowing. In 2024, K1 Investment Management, the leading B2B Enterprise SaaS investor, backed us to accelerate that position further. We are now growing fast, with a proven commercial model spanning both mid-market and enterprise, and a product suite that has become a necessary addition in high-stakes board environments.

The people joining us now will shape how we scale. We are deliberate about how we do that. Our founders and leadership team are deeply invested in keeping the culture that got us here: thoughtful, high calibre, and genuinely human. Ambition and balance are not in competition at Board Intelligence.

If you want to work at the intersection of AI and governance, on problems that matter at the highest level, this is a strong place to be.

Our Mission

We unleash the potential of organisations through the science of board effectiveness, building better businesses and benefitting society.

**The Role

**Juristic is a Danish legal tech company, founded in 2021 and headquartered in Copenhagen. Our platform brings four tools together on the same case data: Structure, Timeline, Flow and JuristIQ, our legal AI in chat and tabular formats.

Clients include PwC, Bird & Bird and Bech-Bruun. Juristic is now part of Board Intelligence, and we are bringing a new product to market. The work is led by our CTO, and we are looking for an AI Engineer to build it with them from the first line of code.

This is a zero-to-one role in a small team of four full-stack developers, a machine learning engineer and the CTO. You will write the code, sit in front of customers, and help decide what we build next.

**Main Responsibilities

**

• Design, build and ship the AI capabilities at the core of a new product, from first prototype to production

• Own LLM-powered workflows end to end, such as document understanding, data extraction and agentic assistants

• Choose and integrate models and providers, and own the prompting, retrieval, evaluation and guardrails that make AI output reliable enough for legal and governance work

• Work directly with customers and the CTO to turn real problems into product decisions, and help own the product roadmap

• Lay the engineering foundations for the new product, including architecture, testing, observability and deployment, so it can scale

• Work with the wider Juristic and Board Intelligence engineering teams, and contribute to AI tooling shared across the suite

**Person Specification

**We are looking for a builder: an experienced AI engineer who has been a technical founder or an early employee at a startup, and who is ready to do it again.

Required Skills and Experience:

• At least four years of professional software engineering experience

• Experience as a technical founder or early employee at a startup, having built a product from the first line of code

• A track record of building and shipping AI or LLM-powered products to real users

• Practical experience with LLM APIs, prompt design, retrieval and evaluating model output in production

• Strong engineering fundamentals across backend and frontend, with the judgement to move fast without leaving a mess behind

• A strong product mindset: you have worked directly with customers and owned a product roadmap

• Hungry, motivated and ready for another zero-to-one journey

• Fluent written and spoken English

Nice to haves:

Experience with our stack: TypeScript (Node.js and React) and Python

Experience with document processing, such as PDF parsing and extraction from unstructured text

Experience building agentic systems, tool use or MCP integrations

Experience with search and retrieval infrastructure, such as Elasticsearch or vector databases

A background in legal tech, governance or B2B SaaS for professional users

What good looks like in this role:

• After three months: you know our customers, the product vision and the codebase, and you have shipped AI features that real users rely on

• After six months: the core AI capabilities of the new product are in production, backed by evaluations that show they are reliable, and you are acting on customer feedback

• After twelve months: the product is in market with paying customers, you are a trusted voice on the roadmap, and the AI foundations you built are reused across the Juristic and Board Intelligence suite

**How We Work

**We hire people who are expert at what they do. Once you join, you have the autonomy to shape how you work and the space to do it well. That doesn’t mean working in isolation. You’ll have colleagues who know their craft, regular collaboration across functions, and easy access to senior leadership when you need it.

We keep our structure flat. We work at pace in an agile, nimble environment where good ideas don’t wait for permission. If you spot something that could work better, we encourage you to say so. If you want to run with an idea, we’ll back you to do it.

We work with people who take pride in their output, back their team through the hard parts, and leave things better than they found them.

**What Happens Next

**Once you apply, our Talent team will review your application. If there’s a fit, they’ll be in touch to discuss the role and next steps.

**How We Use AI In Our Hiring

**We use AI responsibly, both in the software we build for governance teams and in how we hire. Our Talent team may use AI to support application review, CV analysis, or identifying areas that need further verification.

But hiring decisions are made by people. AI surfaces signals; people make the call on whether to progress a candidate or extend an offer.

If you’d like details on how your data is handled during recruitment, contact our Talent team.

**Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

**We’re an equal opportunities employer. We’re building a team that works because it reflects a breadth of experience, background, and perspective.

Apply even if you don’t tick every box on the job specification. If the role excites you and you think you could make an impact, we want to hear from you.

We don’t discriminate on the basis of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. If you need reasonable adjustments at any stage of recruitment, or if there’s anything else we can do to make the process more accessible, tell our Talent team. We’ll sort it.

**Your Safety Matters

**Be cautious of unexpected messages claiming to be from Board Intelligence. We will never ask you for fees as part of recruitment. If you’re unsure whether a communication is genuine, contact our Talent team through our official channels before sharing information or clicking links.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

We are looking for a Product Compliance Manager to join Veo's newly established Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) team.

As Veo continues to grow, we navigate a broad range of regulatory requirements across our products and business, from certifications, product safety, and environmental regulation to market access and broader compliance obligations.

In this role, you will focus on product-related regulatory compliance and certifications, while also working across Veo's broader compliance agenda. You will work closely with colleagues across Hardware, Product Development, Production, Procurement and other parts of the business to understand applicable requirements and help translate them into practical processes and solutions.

You will join a small GRC team with a broad mandate and significant exposure across Veo. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys understanding regulation, technology, and business.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Coordinate Veo's product certification and market-access activities across relevant markets, working closely with Hardware, Production and other internal stakeholders.

• Monitor and assess new and changing regulatory requirements relevant to Veo and help determine their practical implications for our products and business.

• Develop and maintain a structured overview of regulatory and certification requirements applicable to Veo's products throughout their lifecycle.

• Drive and coordinate implementation of regulatory and compliance requirements across relevant business functions, ensuring clear ownership, appropriate documentation and timely follow-up.

• Work with regulatory frameworks relevant to Veo's products, including areas such as product safety, batteries, electrical and electronic equipment, environmental requirements, waste and recycling obligations and related product compliance requirements.

• Coordinate with external certification bodies, laboratories, consultants and other specialists where required.

• Maintain and develop compliance documentation, certification records, technical files, declarations and other evidence required to demonstrate compliance.

• Support the assessment of regulatory and compliance implications when Veo enters new markets, introduces new products or makes material changes to existing products.

• Support Veo's broader compliance activities, including policies, procedures, monitoring, due diligence, risk assessments and training.

• Support customer, auditor and other stakeholder requests relating to compliance and certifications.

• Contribute to the continued development of Veo's broader GRC framework and take part in cross-functional compliance projects as required.

**Your qualifications:

**

• Relevant higher education in engineering, technology, law, business, quality/compliance, or another relevant discipline.

• Relevant professional experience within product compliance, regulatory compliance, certification, quality/regulatory affairs or a similar area, preferably from an international company.

• Experience working with regulatory requirements affecting hardware or electronic products is an advantage.

• Experience with one or more areas such as product safety, product certifications, battery regulation, electrical/electronic equipment regulation, environmental product requirements, waste/recycling regulation or similar regulatory regimes.

• Experience coordinating certification processes, testing, technical documentation, declarations or interactions with certification bodies and laboratories is highly relevant.

• Broader compliance experience, for example within sanctions and export controls, third-party due diligence, anti-bribery and corruption or other corporate compliance areas, is an advantage.

• An ability to understand complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical requirements for technical, operational and commercial teams.

• Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating initiatives across different functions and areas of expertise.

• A structured approach to documentation, monitoring and follow-up, combined with the ability to identify and prioritize material compliance risks.

• Strong business understanding and a pragmatic approach to compliance. You should be comfortable finding solutions that meet regulatory requirements while enabling the business to operate effectively.

• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership in an environment where processes and frameworks are still being developed.

• Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

At Veo, the Governance, Risk & Compliance team provides oversight, coordination and assurance across the company. We work closely with teams throughout Veo to ensure that regulatory requirements and risks are identified, appropriately owned and effectively managed.

You will report to the Head of Governance, Risk & Compliance and will have considerable opportunity to shape how Veo approaches compliance as the company continues to grow.

Contact Martin Eger Larsen one mel@veo.co if you have any questions

Are you passionate about supporting colleagues offshore? Do you want to work in the green offshore wind industry where your skills and expertise will help secure a sustainable future based on renewable energy? Then you might be the Crewing Coordinator we are looking for.

Cadeler is a global partner in offshore wind farm construction and maintenance, and we are part of an industry that is now, more than ever, both relevant and in high demand. As our industry continues to grow, so do we!

**What will you do?

**As our new Crewing Coordinator, you will be in charge of effectively allocating vessel crews and supporting various initiatives for our colleagues offshore. You will support the implementation of policies and procedures while supporting the development of systems in this realm, for both colleagues on and offshore.

**Your Main Tasks Include

**

• Coordinate the scheduling of vessel crews via electronic rotas so personnel are allocated effectively, ensuring manning requirements are met.

• Coordinate the booking of flights, rail tickets, hire cars and hotels for both vessel crew changes (and training courses where necessary).

• Assist the HR/ Head of Marine HR with the induction and initial documentation for offshore crew.

• Support the implementation of recruitment campaigns to source personnel to fill offshore crewing requirements.

• Advise and support project and department manager’s resourcing needs.

• Input data into the HR database and create reports to be analysed by the HR/ Crewing Manager.

The overall purpose of Danish Red Cross’ (DRC) international engagement is to increase and strengthen humanitarian impact, inspire and act for human dignity, and enhance resilience and social cohesion in contexts of poverty, conflict and disaster.

The Global Partnership unit leads the coordination and strategic direction of the Danish Red Cross’ international partnerships, external and within the Red Cross and Red Crescent movement. The Unit is responsible for global resource mobilization efforts and initiatives and provides support to countries and regions. The Unit hosts the Danish Red Cross’ core donor specialization knowledge and capacity on compliance and strategies. Furthermore, the unit supports and quality assures proposals to core donors.

The position

As part of the Movement relations and private partnerships team (MOPS), the Partnership Advisor will drive Danish Red Cross’ strategic engagement with Danish and international foundations and private sector actors, with the objective of growing and diversifying non-institutional funding and strategic partnerships. The role combines new partnership development with strategic management and growth of high-value, multi-year partnerships. It focuses on senior-level relationship building, development of innovative partnership models, negotiation of multi-year agreements, and strong partnership stewardship across the full lifecycle. The Advisor will position DRC as a preferred humanitarian partner among Danish businesses, corporate foundations, family foundations, and selected international private sector actors through collaboration within the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.

Main responsibilities:

• Develop and implement a multi-year strategy for Danish and international private sector and foundation engagement aligned with DRC’s international priorities.

• Build and convert a qualified pipeline of high-value partnership opportunities, with clear income and partnership-growth ambitions.

• Lead the strategic management of one or more high-value, multi-year foundation partnerships, including relationship management, governance, internal coordination, delivery oversight and identification of opportunities for growth.

• Ensure strong partnership stewardship throughout the grant lifecycle, working closely with programme, finance and operational colleagues to support delivery, reporting, compliance and proactive management of risks and partner expectations.

• Develop partnership models beyond traditional grant funding, including strategic co-creation and multi-stakeholder alliances.

• Support country and regional teams to identify, shape and pursue high-potential private sector and foundation partnerships.

• Work closely with Business Development Advisors, Fundraising, and Operations to align private sector engagement with programming priorities.

• Represent DRC in relevant private sector and foundation networks and relevant Movement platforms related to private sector engagement.

We expect you to have the following qualifications:

• A master’s degree or MBA in Business, International Affairs, International Development or related

• Significant experience (7-10 years) in business development, resource mobilization, partnership development, preferably in the humanitarian or non-profit sector

• Demonstrated success in securing high-value, multi-year private sector or foundation partnerships

• Demonstrated experience managing complex, high-value, multi-year and/or multi-stakeholder partnerships including stakeholder engagement, negotiation, renewal and growth

• Strong established network in Denmark and ideally internationally

• Solid understanding of private sector CSR strategies, corporate foundations, and philanthropic trends

• Strong strategic account-management skills, including experience balancing partner expectations with organisational priorities and operational realities

• Experience coordinating complex partnerships across multiple internal teams, technical areas and geographies

• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English, Danish is an advantage

As a person you have the following competences:

• High level of strategic thinking and diplomatic and political judgement

• Ability to lead processes and engage people across functions and geographies

• Results-oriented and entrepreneurial mindset and ability to turn opportunities into concrete action.

• Collaborative team player with the ability to build trust and work in a multicultural environment

We offer

A full-time position of 37 working hours per week in an inspiring workplace. You will have the opportunity to work in a diversified motivated team of donor experts and be part of Danish Red Cross’ large global humanitarian action. You will refer to the Head of Global Partnership in Copenhagen.

The position is based in Copenhagen with potential 4-8-week travel. Salary and employment conditions will comply with Danish Red Cross’s collective bargain agreement with AC.

Application and further information

We look forward to receiving your application via the Red Cross home page www.rodekors.dk/job

In case you have questions to the position please contact Head of Global Partnerships, Marie-Chantal Legendre Dahl mcd@rodekors.dk or Team coordinator Vivian Pucher vipuc@rodekors.dk

Application deadline is 20th November 2026; Interviews will take place soon thereafter. The expected date of commencement is as soon as possible, preferably no later than January 1st.

_

Red Cross

Join us. Together we can make a world of difference. The Red Cross is always present. Then you might be our new student assistant in the International Secretariat at the Danish Red Cross Headquarters in Copenhagen.

The Danish Red Cross’ International Department supports and cooperates with national societies in countries in Africa, the Middle East, Europe, and Asia. As a student assistant in the International Secretariat, you will be part of a dynamic and fast-paced team in the International Department. The primary function of the International Secretariat is to support the International Director and Management Group in lifting strategic and key cross-cutting areas for the benefit of the International Department as well as the Danish Red Cross as a whole. Your assignments

The assignments that the student assistant will be responsible for in the International Secretariat are wide-ranging and will for instance include:

• Assisting the International Secretariat with various tasks relating to the planning, implementation, and follow-up on strategic organisational processes in the International Department

• Assisting with internal communication, including maintaining the International Department’s intranet in English, proofreading documents and drafting PowerPoint presentations in English and Danish, and ensuring the layout of various types of documents

• Assisting with the planning and coordination of high-level meetings and large-scale events in the International Department, including the technical set-up (Teams), meeting files, PowerPoint presentations, minutes, practicalities, and follow-up

• Assisting with research and analysis for different target groups

• Assisting with the daily maintenance of the International Department’s office space and contributing to a nice working environment.

Your profile

• You work independently and proactively, but you are also an active team player. You are always ready to chip in and help with any task that is needed – from the mundane to the novel – that working in a dynamic and fast-paced International Secretariat requires.

• You have excellent communication skills in English and Danish (written and verbal), preferably with a proven record of communication to various target groups. You are also familiar with Teams platforms and other digital communication tools – and you are ready to dive into new communication tools if needed.

• You can give concrete examples of your organizational skills and experience, perhaps in relation to meetings/events, and preferably from other student jobs or voluntary work where your contributions made a real difference.

• As you will work in an ever-changing environment that demands high accuracy, you must be well-structured, thorough, reliable, punctual, and flexible.

• With a curious mindset and a drive for new challenges, you also proactively suggest improvements both within and beyond your own responsibilities.

You will get the chance to gain first-hand experience of what it is like to work in the International Secretariat that supports the International Director and International Management Group. **WHY WORK AT JOE & THE JUICE

**JOE & THE JUICE is a people-centric food and beverage company built around culture, offering much more than just juice, sandwiches, and coffee.

We believe in four simple virtues that shape everything we do:

• Positive Attitude

• Inclusion

• Social Ties

• Growth

For us, this means that when you choose a cup-half-full mindset, welcome people from every background, build real friendships across the teams by creating or helping create great guest experiences, and use every day as a chance to learn something new, you become more than just a Juicer or staff member; like us, you continue to search and find purpose and meaning in what you do.

From your first day, you'll be part of an international network of people who support each other, celebrate wins together, and push each other to grow. You'll learn by doing and move through our Moneyball career path—our internal system that tracks your performance and fast-tracks you toward promotion. Most of our leaders have earned their stripes behind the bar (fun fact: over 75% of our employees started as Juicers!), so you will always be part of a company built on that same journey. If you love a fast-paced environment, music, and people, and you like the idea of turning a job into a lifestyle, JOE can become a place to build skills, friendships, and a career that takes you across cities, countries, and roles.

**JOB SUMMARY

**The Global Talent Management Lead is responsible for setting the standard for how JOE identifies, develops and moves talent, ensuring that internal mobility and leadership readiness are predictable, data-driven and scalable across the organization. The role owns the talent review and development planning approach for operational and office-based roles, the talent management system and pipeline reporting, and partners with Culture, Performance & Reward, Operations, People Business Partners and regional T&LD to shape decisions on where and how talent is built. As part of the Talent & Leadership Development team within People & Development, this position is critical to the ambition of filling 90% of leadership roles from within, supporting JOE's purpose and growth ambitions.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**

• Set the company-wide standard for talent development, owning a regular and objective talent review process for operational and office-based roles, anchored in individual development plans.

• Shape and own the roll-out of the talent development model, starting with operational roles from Juicer to Store Manager and scaling quickly to office-based roles, with SOPs that work consistently across all regions.

• Own the strategy, selection and implementation of the talent management system, ensuring it connects with shared learning platforms and provides one source of truth for talent data.

• Own pipeline reporting and insight - internal fill rate, successor coverage, development plan completion and employee development experience - informing strategic people and growth decisions at leadership level.

• Ensure pipeline gaps are identified early and closed across all regions, steering gap-closing actions with People Business Partners and regional T&LD.

• Own visible career pathways and promotion criteria across the organization, so employees can see their next step from day one.

• Partner with Culture, Performance & Reward and Operations to set aligned leadership standards, competency framework and people cycle, acting as the organization's thought leader on talent development.

• Contribute to pipeline-fill initiatives, such as structured mentoring, that turn talent review outcomes into concrete development actions.

**WHO YOU ARE

**

• Passionate about developing talent. A standard-setter who builds career pathways and talent development processes that work the same way in every region and every role

• Data-led: you turn pipeline numbers into insight that leaders act on

• Operationally credible: you understand how careers are built from the bar to the office

• A partner who influences across Culture, Performance & Reward, Operations, People Business Partners and regional T&LD without needing authority

• A thought leader who works with high autonomy and shapes how we build leaders

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING

**

• 7+ years in talent management, talent development or people development roles, ideally in global multi-site quick service restaurant, retail or similar front line heavy industry

• Proven track record owning talent review-, succession planning- and individual development plan processes

• Experience selecting and implementing a talent management system, incl. integration with learning platforms

• Strong analytical skills: pipeline reporting, internal fill rate and successor coverage

• Experience designing competency frameworks, career pathways and promotion criteria

• Experience rolling out global processes and SOPs across regions and markets

• Fluent in English - other languages are a bonus

**OUR BENEFITS

**We offer a benefits package that includes a paid pension plan, health insurance, parental leave, and additional vacation. Besides that, we provide some JOE-ified benefits:

• Our global headquarters is conveniently located in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, where over 200 friendly faces come together!

• Fantastic office facilities, including a fully staffed JOE & THE JUICE bar, where we serve delicious breakfast, daily lunch, refreshing juices, and top-notch barista coffee.

• At JOE, we embrace a flat hierarchy that values every opinion, creating a welcoming space for your ideas and suggestions to thrive.

• Lively monthly social calendar filled with fun activities like running club, wine tasting, creative evenings, and Friday bars - there's always something exciting happening!

• As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to take on a BTC (Behind the Counter) shift in one of our bars twice a year, adding a unique touch to your experience.

**Ready to turn a job into a lifestyle?

****ABOUT JOE & THE JUICE

**Founded in Copenhagen in 2002, JOE & THE JUICE has grown into a global fast-casual concept with more than 500 locations across 25+ countries and over 7,000 employees worldwide, with our sights set on 1,000 stores by 2028.

Our people-centric culture and sustainability agenda are part of our Nordic heritage, and remain central to our commitment to a better future. Along the way, internal workshops and mentorship sharpen your skills, while exchange programs and international assignments can take you across our markets.

Ready to embark on this exciting journey? Apply today and become a part of JOE & THE JUICE!
